title: "Sorting, Range Queries, and Monotonic Structures"
description: "A connected learning path through 11 worked algorithms topics."

## What you are really learning

Order values and maintain just enough information to answer repeated range questions.

The goal is not to learn 11 unrelated definitions. Compare the operations needed by each classic problem and notice which invariant survives from one technique to the next.

## Begin with a small example

Merge sort splits values into halves then combines two sorted halves.

$$
T(n)=2T(n/2)+cn
$$

**What the symbols mean:** T(n) is work for n entries; 2 counts recursive calls for each half; c is per-element merging cost.

**Substitute actual numbers:** For n=8,c=1, three merge levels each handle eight entries, giving about 8×3=24 merge-work units. The point is the number of levels, not a particular CPU time.

This is how the topic pages below should be read: understand the numbers first, then generalise to the equation.

## The chapters in this family

1. **[Sorting](../sorting/index.qmd)** — Reorder a collection according to a comparison rule.
2. **[Merge Sort](../merge-sort/index.qmd)** — Recursively sort halves and merge their ordered outputs.
3. **[Counting Sort](../counting-sort/index.qmd)** — Count discrete keys in a bounded domain to construct sorted output.
4. **[Bucket Sort](../bucket-sort/index.qmd)** — Distribute keys into buckets, sort locally, and concatenate.
5. **[Radix Sort](../radix-sort/index.qmd)** — Sort positional digits with a stable subroutine.
6. **[Monotonic Stack](../monotonic-stack/index.qmd)** — Maintain candidate indices whose values follow a monotonic invariant.
7. **[Monotonic Queue](../monotonic-queue/index.qmd)** — Maintain an ordered deque of undominated candidates in a sliding window.
8. **[Prefix Sum](../prefix-sum/index.qmd)** — Precompute cumulative aggregates for efficient interval queries.
9. **[Segment Tree](../segment-tree/index.qmd)** — Store associative aggregates over a recursively partitioned range.
10. **[Binary Indexed Tree](../binary-indexed-tree/index.qmd)** — Represent prefix aggregates through binary-indexed intervals.
11. **[Sweep Line](../sweep-line/index.qmd)** — Process geometric or time events in sorted order while maintaining active state.

## Practice method

Choose ONE chapter. Reproduce its example with paper and pencil, identify what is cached or discarded, implement the tiny idea, and explain one case in which the algorithm's assumptions fail. Repeat until the invariant feels natural.

The [original executable examples](../examples/README.md) provide code you can run and test. If two topics seem similar, compare them in the [algorithm selection guide](../guides/choose-a-pattern.qmd).
